conventions.convention: Dirac Clifford multiplication satisfies c(ξ)c(η)+c(η)c(ξ)=−2g⁻¹(ξ,η)I, is skew-Hermitian and odd, and D=Σ c(eⁱ)∇eᵢ. The Hermitian metric is linear in its first variable.
Spin lifts use right principal bundles and the full-even Euclidean Spin group in the positive real Clifford convention v²=|v|². Ranks n≥1 are required; no rank-zero torsor convention is imposed.
The negative-square spinor action is c₀=i c₊ and chirality is Γ=iᵐc₀(e¹)⋯c₀(e²ᵐ). Relative to the positive-action volume convention, half-spin labels exchange when m is odd.
Curvature is R(X,Y)=[∇X,∇Y]−∇[X,Y], and Rm(X,Y,Z,W)=g(R(X,Y)Z,W). The spin-curvature action is one quarter of Σ Rmᵢⱼₐᵦcₐcᵦ; the twisting term sums over i<j.
A-hat is det½((iΩLC/4π)/sinh(iΩLC/4π)), with constant-term-one formal square root. The relative character is strW exp(−F(V/S)/(2πi)); an ungraded twist uses ordinary trace.

At a zero-dimensional point of orientation ε, the reference Clifford line has grading εI and the multiplicity grading is εΓV. Thus the relative character is ε(dim V⁺−dim V⁻); signed integration contributes a second ε.
The compact positive-dimensional Dirac realization has exact domain H¹, and its square has domain H². Index conclusions require compactness without boundary and concern the complex Fredholm index.
The Euclidean Fourier transform uses the negative-sign 2π normalization, so D transforms to multiplication by 2πi c(ξ).

load_bearing.statement: Assuming full AC, near a point of a closed even-dimensional geometric Clifford module, the heat transport coefficients have Getzler degree at most 2j; the leading operator is the stated formal curvature oscillator. For n=2m the diagonal supertrace coefficients vanish for j<m, and the j=m coefficient is determined by its heat equation.
Assume full AC and the closed hypotheses of the heat-trace lemma. For every r,b,N≥0 there is J such that the cutoff heat parametrix satisfies ‖Kₜ−Hⱼ(t)‖CˣʳCʸᵇ ≤ Cᵣ,ᵦ,ₙ tᴺ for 0<t≤1.

Assume full AC. A supplied Spin lift produces a smooth Hermitian graded Clifford bundle with compatible spin connection. Every graded Hermitian Clifford module locally factors as S₀ tensor W; the relative curvature and multiplicity supertrace have global transition laws. For a product spinor twist the relative curvature is Fᴱ.
Assume full AC. For the stated geometric Clifford module, F(V/S) commutes with Clifford multiplication and D²=∇*∇+scal/4+Σᵢ<ⱼ c(eⁱ)c(eʲ)F(V/S)ᵢⱼ. The positive-frequency principal symbol is |ξ|²I.

Assume full AC and closed Riemannian M of even dimension n≥2. The closure domain of D equals H¹ and its maximal distributional L² domain; its graph norm is equivalent to H¹, smooth sections are a core, and the closure is selfadjoint.

Assume full AC. On a closed even-dimensional geometric Clifford module, e^(−tD²) is trace class with smooth kernel for t>0, its diagonal series and derivatives converge uniformly, and its supertrace equals the complex chiral index and the integral of the diagonal supertrace.

Assume full AC. An oriented Euclidean smooth real bundle of rank n≥1 over a Hausdorff second-countable smooth manifold admits a Spin lift iff w₂(E)=0. When nonempty, isomorphism classes of lifts form an H¹(M;F₂) torsor under twisting by principal sign bundles.

Assume full AC. For a compact boundaryless oriented Riemannian manifold of even dimension 2m, m≥0, and a finite-rank graded Hermitian Clifford module with compatible connection, D⁺:H¹(V⁺)→L²(V⁻) is Fredholm and ind(D⁺)=∫M[A-hat(TM) ch(V/S)]₂ₘ, with the stated zero-dimensional reference grading.

alerts.finding: In thm-complex-spin-modules-and-compact-reducibility, step 1.1 chooses a 'pairwise orthogonal anisotropic real basis e_1,...,e_n' and separately defines normalized vectors u_i=e_i/sqrt(|Q(e_i)|). Step 2.1 nevertheless says 'Set ω=i^m e_1⋯e_{2m}; the Clifford relations show ω²=1' and uses p_±=(1±ω)/2 as idempotents. For the positive quadratic convention actually fixed here, ω²=∏ Q(e_i), which need not be 1 for that chosen basis. In dimension two, taking e_1=(2,0), e_2=(0,1) gives ω²=4 and the displayed p_± are not idempotents. This is a false intermediate computation in the supplier proof; it does not disprove its stated half-spin dimension theorem.

seams_checked.note: Checked the supplier's full-even Euclidean group, central double cover, local logarithm section, universal-cover rank range and complex spinor dimensions against their actual consumer uses. The consumer explicitly translates c₀=i c₊ and the resulting chirality-label change, preserves the n≥3 universal-cover restriction, and treats ranks one and two separately. The reverse comparison found no stronger consumer attribution than the supplier Statements. The supplier proof's unnormalized volume-element computation is recorded separately in alerts.
